topic: Why you can hold your breath longer the second time
narration: Your lungs lie to you. Most people think that burning urge to breathe means oxygen is running out. It doesn't. That urge is triggered by carbon dioxide, and your first attempt flushes it out of your blood. When you hold your breath, carbon dioxide piles up, turning your blood acidic, and sensors in your brainstem sound the alarm. So round two starts with carbon dioxide already low, while your spleen squeezes out extra red blood cells. You can black out before that alarm ever sounds.
